plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes crowded with fragrant violet-blue blossoms. Fields hum with bees and glow in soft purple waves. The scent drifts across the countryside on warm summer afternoons.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August, usually peaking in July
plants.location: Provence, France, and other Mediterranean-climate regions of southern Europe
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with lavender.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems carry huge golden-petaled heads that turn their faces toward the sun. Each head is packed with a spiral of tiny florets at its dark center. Whole fields of them make a bright yellow sea in midsummer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midsummer to early autumn, with many fields in full bloom in mid-July
plants.location: Great Plains and Midwest of the United States, plus Europe's sunflower belt
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is made up of hundreds to thousands of tiny individual flowers. The seeds form in a spiral pattern that follows the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Large, cup-shaped blooms rise on tall stalks above round leaves that bead water like polished jade. The pink-tipped petals open at dawn in still ponds. Their sweet scent draws beetles into the flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, with peak bloom from June to August
plants.location: Ponds and wetlands across Asia, including China, Japan and India
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a microscopic texture that sheds water and dirt, which is known as the 'lotus effect'. The flower can also hold its temperature at about 30–35°C as it blooms.
